State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
State Bank Of India vs Herambh Chintamani Joshi on 28 March, 2022
1 A/1616/2019

 Date of filing :02.12.2019
 Date of order :28.03.2022

 MAHARASHTRA STATE CONSUMER DISPUTE
 REDRESSAL COMMISSION,MUMBAI, BENCH AT
 AURANGABAD.

FIRST APPEAL NO. : 1616 OF 2019
IN COMPLAINT CASE NO.: 309 OF 2019
DISTRICT CONSUMER FORUM : AURANGABAD.

1. State Bank of India,
Through Regional Manager,
RBO, Region-I, Zoee Aurangabad.

2. The Br. Manager,
State Bank of India, Ramdas Tower Branch,
Pundlik Nagar road, Aurangabad. APPELLANTS.

 VERSUS

Herambha Chintamani Joshi,
R/o Flat No.3, Ekdanant Residency,
Alanakar society, Garkheda,
Aurangabad. RESPONDENT

 CORAM :Smt.S.T.Barne, Hon'ble Presiding Judicial
 Member.
 Mr.K.M.Lawande, Hon'ble Member.

 Present : Adv.V.B.Kulkarni for appellant,
 Adv.N.K.Tungar for respondent.

 JUDGMENT
(Delivered on 28/03/2022)
 2 A/1616/2019

Per Smt.S.T.Barne, Hon'ble Presiding Judicial Member.
1. The appellant State Bank of India has preferred this
appeal against the judgment and order in C.C.No.
309/2019 decided by District Consumer Forum,
Aurangabad on 5.11.2019.
2. The appellant are the opponents and the respondent
Herambh Chintamani Joshi is the complainant in the
original consumer complaint before District Consumer
Forum. Hence, they are hereinafter referred as per their
status in the complaint.
3. It is the case of complainant that, he is having his
saving account with opponent no.2. On 29.10.2018 the
complainant had been to Shirdi. He has withdrawn
amount of Rs.5,000/- through ATM of Andhra Bank, at
Shirdi. There was no security guard at said ATM centre.
Then he went to Temple of Shirdi. On 30.10.2018 the
complainant received SMS from State Bank of India that
transaction are carried out by using ATM card and total
amount of Rs. 1,57,800/- was transferred and withdrawn
from his account. The complainant went to Shirdi police
station. However, the police told him that, his account is at
Aurangabad, he is required to lodge FIR at Aurangabad.
His written complaint was taken and certificate was issued
to him by police Inspector on 30.10.2018, to that effect.
The complainant has also informed his daughter at
Aurangabad to approach to opponent no.2 Bank and to
block the card. On 30.10.2018 his ATM card was blocked.
The complaint also lodged report with opponent no.2 as to
 3 A/1616/2019

ATM transaction dispute. The complainant thereupon
obtained details of transaction from opponent no.2. The
complainant came to know that, unknown person did
unauthorised use of his ATM card for 6 times. The amount
of Rs.40,000/- each was transferred thrice and amount of
Rs. 75,000/- withdrawn by cash from his account. The
complainant requested the opponent to put hold on those
bank accounts to which amount was transferred. The
opponent informed the complainant that, he was not
having ATM card with him at the time of lodging complaint.
Hence, his claim for unauthorised transaction is rejected by
the opponent. Hence, due to alleged deficiency in service
on the part of opponent and not adopting RBI guidelines
the complainant has filed consumer complaint.
4. The opponent no.1&2 have filed their written
statement before District Consumer Forum. The copy of
said w.s. is at page no. 53 to 62 of appeal compilation. The
opponent admitted that, the complainant is having his
saving account no. 62297600542 with opponent no.2
branch and that the opponent no.2 has issued ATM card
no. 521108000932229 on his request and as per terms &
conditions of the bank. The bank has also issued
guidelines for the use of ATM Debit card. The points
regarding loss of card also clarified i.e. to keep separate
note of card and the associated account number, in a place
readily accessible. The card holder should immediately to
block the card through the available channels(i.e. through
sms /internet banking SBI anywhere mobile App, SBi
Quick mobile application, SBI branch etc.) The card holder
 4 A/1616/2019

is responsible for security of the card. If the cardholder has
not completed with financial liability on the lost of or stolen
card would rest with the card holder.
5. It is the contention of opponent that, it is obligatory
on cardholder not to allow anyone else to use his card or to
share his PIN or password or other security information. At
the time of transaction the ATM card was with
complainant. the complainant failed to safeguard the ATM
card/debit card, which led to disputed transaction. Hence,
opponent cannot be held liable for this loss occurred.
6. The complainant placed reliance upon the copy of
certificate issued by police about his lodging of FIR on
31.10.2018. The complaint, lodged with opponent as ATM
dispute. The information obtained from opponent about
transaction, the copy of statement of account of complaint,
copy of RBI circular dated 6th July 2017. The letter dated
14.3.2019 issued by opponent no.2 to the complainant
rejecting the claim of complainant for unauthorised
transaction on his account of Rs.1,57,800/-.
7. On giving opportunity to both the parties of hearing
the Ld. District Consumer Forum pleased to allow the
complaint by awarding amount of Rs. 1,57,800/- with 9 %
from 30.10.2018 till realisation of the amount of cost of
proceeding Rs. 3,000/-.
8. Therefore, the opponents SBI branch has preferred
this appeal on the following grounds.
5 A/1616/2019

 That, the District Consumer Forum has ignored
grounds that the complainant has used the ATM card and
withdrawn the amount by using card. The District
Consumer Forum has decided the complaint in
hypothetical manner. The complainant has not followed
the instructions issued while issuing ATM card/debit card
to the complainant. He has not complied the terms and
conditions to secure the ATM card and pin. The
complainant could have used the sms, internet banking,
mobile App to block the card. The present case is relating
to negligence on the part of complainant. However, the
District Consumer Forum allowed the claim of complainant
by relying upon the RBI circular. The District Consumer
Forum relied upon the statement that the complainant has
received sms on 30.10.2019. However, there is no evidence
adduced by the complainant in its support. It is also not
the case of unauthorised transaction, it is related to
negligence of complainant. Hence, the opponent/appellant
has prayed for setting aside the order of District Consumer
Forum.
9. In view of respective submissions of the parties
following points arise for our determination. We have noted
them along with our findings against it for the reasons to
follow.
Sr. Points. Findings.
No.
1 Whether, the complainant Yes.
 proves that, there is deficiency
 in service on the part of
 opponents?
 6 A/1616/2019

2 Whether, there requires No.
 interference in the order of
 District Consumer Forum?
3 What order? As per final order.

 REASONING
Point Nos.1&2 :-
10. It reveals from record that this appeal is presented by
appellant through Adv.V.B.Kulkarni on 7.12.2019. The
appeal is admitted on 16.12.2019 and adjourned for notice
to respondent after admission. On the same day stay to
impugned order granted subject to depositing entire
amount as per award within 4 weeks. However, on
7.2.2020 the appellant submitted application seeking
extension of time. Hence, one week extension was granted
to deposit amount. However, the appellant not turned up
to give intimation. Thus, matter was adjourned to secure
presence of respondent and submission of written notes of
arguments. On 12.1.2021 the respondent gave appearance
and submitted that he has not received copy of appeal
compilation, there upon the directions were issued to
appellant to supply copy of appeal compilation to the
respondent. However, the Adv. for appellant not appeared
since then though matter was adjourned for submission of
written notes of arguments. Then due to pandemic
situation out of Covid-19, the matter adjourned from time
to time. On 26.9.2021 the appellant was absent when the
matter was posted for submission of written notes of
arguments. The opponent and his Advocate was present.
The opponent raised objection that he is the senior citizen
 7 A/1616/2019

and appellant is prolonging the matter. He has make his
submissions & supported the judgment of District
Consumer Forum. Then matter adjourned to 27.1.2022
matter adjourned to decide on the basis of record due to
absence of appellant since long. On 27.1.2022 also
appellant remained absent. On 14.2.2022 due to directions
of Hon'ble State Commission the bench formation was not
available matter adjourned to 28.2.1011 on 28.2.2022, the
appellant was absent, the Commission was busy in
deciding old matters. Hence, matter was adjourned to
7.3.2022. On 7.3.2022 for want of Corum, the matter
adjourned to 28.3.2022. On this date also appellant
remained absent. Hence, as the matter is pending since
long and respondent is attending every date, the appal is
decided on the basis of record.
11. It reveals from record that, both the parties have
submitted their respective pleadings along with documents,
relied upon by them specified in their respective pleading.
Both the parties have almost relied upon same documents
and RBI circular. Most of the facts are not disputed.
12. It is not disputed that, complainant is having his
saving account with opponent bank bearing account no.
62297600542 . The opponent bank has issued to him
ATM/Debit card on his request, on terms and conditions.
According to complainant on 29.11.2018 he had been to
Shirdi. On that day he has withdrawn amount of Rs.
5,000/- through ATM centre, of Bank of Andhra at Shirdi.
Then he went to Shirdi temple. In the said rush, his ATM
 8 A/1616/2019

card was lost. He received sms messages from opponent
no.2 bank on 30.11.2018 about disbursement of amount
from his account. He has not used the card. Therefore, he
informed to his daughter to approach the opponent no.2
bank to block the card and his card was blocked. The
complaint has also lodged report with Shirdi police station.
It has issued certificate to the complainant. He has
obtained details of transaction from opponent bank and his
amount of Rs. 1,57,000/- found to have been debited.
13. It is not disputed by opponent that, the card was
blocked on 30.11.2018. Therefore, the fact that, the bank
has received information of unauthorised transactions from
complainant on 30.11.2018 is not disputed. The
complainant placed reliance of RBI, circular in relation to
unauthorised transaction and claimed that as per said
circular he has given intimation to opponent bank
immediately on 30.11.2018 within 7 days. Hence, the
opponent was supposed to reversed the amounts to the
account of complainant.
14. The opponent in their pleadings submitted that, from
the certificate issued by police station it reveals that,
alleged transaction took place on 29th & 30th Nov. 2018,
when the complainant was having card with him. It is
mentioned in the certificate that, the card is lost on
31.11.2018. All the transactions about which the details
are issued, are prior to the lost of the ATM card.
9 A/1616/2019
15. From the admitted facts it reveals that, the
complainant has used his card on 29.11.2018 for
withdrawal of amount of Rs.5,000/-. Therefore, his card
was lost and he has lodged report on 30.11.2018. Then he
received sms from opponent bank about debiting of
amount from his account by ATM. He has not used the
ATM after withdrawal of Rs. 5,000/-. Moreover, his
contention that he has blocked the card on 30.11.2018, is
supported by contents in FIR and details of transactions
issued by opponent no.2 bank.
16. It is alleged by the complainant that, he received
information of debit of amount on 30.11.2018 and then he
informed to his daughter to block the card, if the sms alert
would have been received by him, he would have informed
to block the card immediately.
17. The opponent bank submitted in the appeal memo
that the appellant besides his bare statement not produced
the documents to show that, he did not receive message
from opponent till 30.11.2018 about disbursement of
amount. In fact, if at all the bank has issued intimation he
could have produced the record to that effect. The
complainant is not supposed to prove the negative fact
that, when he has not received sms up to 30.11.2018 about
disbursement of amount.
18. Secondly, according to opponent the complainant was
having ATM card with him he might have showed the pin.
Hence, he himself negligent for loss of amount sustained.
10 A/1616/2019

It is important to note that, the complainant himself
claiming that he has used the card for withdrawal of Rs.
5,000/- on 29.11.2018 and then his card lost and he has
not used it. But his amount is disbursed unauthorisedly
and therefore, immediately he lodged report with police &
with opponent. If at all he would have shared the ATM
information or pin, he would not have come forward to
lodge report with police. He is senior citizen, he has shown
his due diligent in lodging report in giving intimation to
opponent to block the card immediately. Therefore, it is not
acceptable that, there is negligence on the part of
complainant either by sharing intimation or pin.
19. On the contrary when he came to know about the
transaction, he has immediately given information to bank
to block the card. In fact, he has also obtained details of
transaction from opponent bank, he found the details of the
transaction of account to which the amounts were
transferred. The opponent bank ought to have investigated
through its machinery into those transactions and could
have revert the amounts. It is not the case of opponent
that, opponent in their investigation into transaction found
that, the complainant has shared the card or information to
that effect. Hence, without any such inquiry or report, it
cannot be said that, complainant himself is responsible for
sharing his ATM information or PIN. Hence, it is not a case
of negligence on the part of complainant, but it happened
due to lost of ATM card.
11 A/1616/2019
20. On perusal of record and judgment of the District
Consumer Forum we are of the opinion that the District
Consumer Forum by relying upon the RBI circular and
considering the fact and circumstances of complainant's
case has rightly held that the opponent no.2 has not given
sms alert message about transaction immediately to the
complainant. Therefore, it has caused delay to block the
card. The opponent has also not followed the RBI
guidelines, for further action. Hence, there appears no
illegality in the judgment of District Consumer Forum.
Hence, we answer the points accordingly and pass following
order.
ORDER
1. Appeal is dismissed.
2. No order as to costs.
Mr.K.M.Lawande Smt.S.T.Barne,
 Member Presiding Judicial Member

UNK
